items.prompt: White to move. The b4 pawn attacks the knight on c3. Where does the knight go?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Na4.
Nce2 is worse than Na4 by at least 15 centipawns.
After Na4 the queen on d2 attacks the b4 pawn.

hints: The knight must leave c3, but where it goes should help another piece too.
Look at the diagonal from d2 to b4. What stands on c3 now?
A knight move to the rim that opens that diagonal for the queen.
items.explain: The knight steps to a4, out of the pawn's reach. That also opens the diagonal from d2, so the queen now attacks the b4 pawn. Black must react at once. At depth 16 Na4 is the engine's first choice and Nce2 is behind it.

feedback_by_move.c3e2: The knight is safe on e2, but it does not open the queen's diagonal, so the b4 pawn stays safe.
feedback_by_move.c3b1: The knight goes home, loses time and gives Black a free move.

items.prompt: Black to move. White has opened the a-file. Black's centre pawns stand on d6 and e6. What does Black play?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...d5.
...Be7 is worse than ...d5 by at least 50 centipawns.
After ...d5 two black units attack the e4 pawn (the d5 pawn and the knight on f6).
After ...d5 only one white unit defends e4 (the pawn on f3).

hints: White's pieces point at the queenside. Where can Black strike that White cannot ignore?
Count the attackers and defenders of the e4 pawn after a central pawn move.
A central pawn move to d5.
items.explain: The pawn leaves d6 for d5. Now the e4 pawn is attacked twice (by that pawn and by the knight on f6) and defended once (by f3), and the bishop on b7 lines up behind d5. White must answer in the centre before the a-file play gets going. At depth 16 ...d5 is the first choice and the quiet ...Be7 lags well behind.

feedback_by_move.f8e7: A natural developing move, but it lets White continue the attack: the engine rates it clearly behind ...d5.
feedback_by_move.g7g6: Another slow move; White keeps the initiative.

items.prompt: Black to move. Which move do you choose? Two of the options are about equally good; one is clearly worse.

claims.statement: ...dxe4 and ...e5 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top move (depth 16).
...Bd6 (Nakamura - Grandelius) is worse than ...dxe4 by at least 40 centipawns.
A white pawn stands on e4.

hints: The pawn on d5 attacks something. Is it protected enough?
Opening the centre favours the side with active pieces. Whose bishop looks better?
A pawn takes a pawn, or a pawn takes space in the centre.
items.explain: Two moves are within a third of a pawn of the best: ...dxe4 opens the long diagonal for the bishop on b7, and ...e5 takes space and blocks White's bishop. ...Bd6 is clearly behind. Nakamura won his game with White anyway: a result is not an evaluation.

feedback_by_move.f8d6: Nakamura - Grandelius continued this way and White won; the engine rates ...Bd6 clearly behind ...dxe4.
feedback_by_move.e6e5: Bok - Gordievsky (the game): playable, within a third of a pawn of the best.

items.prompt: White to move after 16...Rc8. Black threatens to open the centre with ...dxe4. Which moves are playable?

claims.statement: Bc5, Nc5 and Bd3 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top move (depth 16).

hints: Count White's loose pieces: which pieces have no defender?
Black threatens to open the long diagonal. Which White move trades a defender or removes a target?
A bishop or knight move to c5, or developing the bishop.
items.explain: The knights on h6 and a4 are far from the king, and Black threatens ...dxe4 with lines opened for the bishops. A move to c5 trades pieces and removes a target; the game move Bd3 develops and is also within 40 cp of the best at depth 16. The engine's ranking of these three moves changes with search depth, so treat them as playable, not as a mistake.

feedback_by_move.e4d5: Releases the tension in Black's favour.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn on f3 threatens to take on g2. What stops it?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers gxf3.
Rhe1 (the game move) is worse than gxf3 by at least 40 centipawns.

hints: Black's pawn is two steps from queening. What can remove it?
Take the pawn that is closest to promotion before it takes you.
A pawn captures on f3.
items.explain: The pawn on f3 is one capture away from reaching g2 and attacking the rook on h1. Taking it with the g-pawn at once removes the threat. The game move Rhe1 developed a rook but let Black capture on g2 with a lasting advantage. At depth 16 gxf3 is the first choice and Rhe1 is behind by almost a pawn.

feedback_by_move.h1e1: The game move: the engine rates it almost a pawn behind gxf3, and the pawn on g2 stays for the rest of the game.
feedback_by_move.f2e3: Also leaves the pawn in place.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's pawn is on g2 and the two queens face each other on the d-file. Find the only move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Qxd5.
Nd3 (the game move) is worse than Qxd5 by at least 150 centipawns.

hints: Look at what attacks the black queen. Is a trade possible?
The pawn on g2 is the problem; trading queens reduces the danger.
The queen takes the queen on d5.
items.explain: The black queen on d5 is attacked by the white queen along the file, and Black's queen attacks White's. Taking first trades the queens and removes Black's most active piece. The game move Nd3 allowed ...Ne4 with a winning attack. At depth 16 Qxd5 is the engine's only good move.

feedback_by_move.b2d3: The game move: Black answers ...Ne4 and the engine rates the position as lost for White.

items.prompt: Black to move after 11.c4. The pawn on c4 controls b5. What breaks the bind?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...b5.
...a5 is worse than ...b5 by at least 20 centipawns.
After ...b5 the c4 pawn attacks the b5 pawn.

hints: Which Black pawn move challenges White's grip on b5?
The pawn will be taken. What does Black get for it?
A pawn move to b5.
items.explain: The b-pawn steps up to b5 and offers a pawn trade: after cxb5 axb5 Black has opened the a-file and put a pawn on b5, which frees the knight and takes space. White's grip on the queenside is broken. At depth 16 ...b5 is the engine's first choice and the passive ...a5 trails.

feedback_by_move.a6a5: Keeps b5 under control but gives up counterplay; the engine rates it behind ...b5.

items.prompt: White to move after 23...c4. The position is about level. Which queen move keeps it level?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Qb1 or Qf3.
Qc2 (the game move) is worse than Qb1 or Qf3 by at least 150 centipawns.

hints: Count the attackers of b3 before you move the queen.
The black rook, the c-pawn and the bishop on f4 all pull at White's position. Which queen square keeps b3 and the king covered?
The queen steps back to the first rank or to f3.
items.explain: The black c-pawn and rook attack b3, and the bishop on f4 eyes h2. A queen move to b1 or f3 keeps the b3 pawn covered and the king safe. The game move Qc2 walked into a double attack. At depth 16 Qb1 and Qf3 are close to the best; Qc2 lost the game.

feedback_by_move.d3c2: The game move: after ...Qxf5 White loses material and the engine rates the position as lost.

items.prompt: Black to move. The b2 pawn is attacked and White has not defended it. Should Black take?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...Qxb2.
...Qc7 is worse than ...Qxb2 by at least 30 centipawns.
The black queen attacks b2.

hints: Count what White gets after the capture before you judge.
The queen can come back via a3. Is there a way for White to trap it?
The queen captures b2.
items.explain: The queen takes the pawn and, after Rb1, goes to a3 where it is safe. White gains time for an attack, but Black has no direct danger, so the pawn is worth taking. At depth 16 the capture is the engine's first choice. Compare it with the greedy grab that fails in the next lesson.

feedback_by_move.b6c7: Gives up the pawn, but also gives White time: the engine rates it worse than taking.
feedback_by_move.b8c6: Lets White play Nb3 with a good game.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's queen is on a3 and most black pieces are still at home. Which move makes the most of that? (Several are fine.)

claims.statement: f5, Bxf6 and e5 are each within 50 cp of the engine's top move (depth 16); f5 is first.
Be2 (Caruana's move) is worse than f5 by at least 30 centipawns.
Black's queen stands on a3.

hints: Count Black's undeveloped pieces. Only the queen is out.
Opening a line quickly might hit them before they develop.
A pawn move that opens a line (f5 or e5), or a bishop capture.
items.explain: White has a lead in development and can open lines before Black catches up. The pawn on f4 can advance to f5, the pawn on e4 can push to e5 (played 45 times in our master file), or the bishop can take on f6. Caruana played the quieter Be2 and still won; the engine rates it behind these choices (f5 first; Bxf6 and e5 within half a pawn), but a result is not an evaluation.

feedback_by_move.f1e2: Caruana's move: the engine rates it behind f5 and Bxf6, yet he won.

items.prompt: Black to move. Two pawns can take the knight on d5. Which one?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers ...cxd5.
...exd5 (the game move) is worse than ...cxd5 by at least 80 centipawns.
Two black pawns (c6 and e6) attack d5.

hints: Compare the two pawn structures that result. Which one keeps the e-file closed?
After ...exd5 the pawn is gone from e6. What does the white pawn on e5 do next?
The c-pawn takes.
items.explain: Black can take with either pawn. Taking with the e-pawn clears e6, so the white pawn on e5 can advance to e6 with a strong attack. Taking with the c-pawn keeps the e-file closed and the king safe. At depth 16 ...cxd5 is the engine's first choice and ...exd5 loses more than a pawn.

feedback_by_move.e6d5: The game move. White answered e6! and Black's king never got safe; the engine rates ...exd5 at least 0.8 pawns behind ...cxd5.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's e-pawn has captured on d5. Find the strike.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers e6.
O-O is worse than e6 by at least 80 centipawns.
After e6 two black pieces attack the pawn on e6.

hints: The e5 pawn is passed and has an open file. What does it threaten?
Advancing it creates a threat of capture on f7 and takes e6 away from the king.
The pawn moves one square.
items.explain: The pawn on e5 is passed and can advance to e6, where it attacks f7 and cannot be captured profitably. It also opens the diagonal for the bishop on e2. Quiet moves like O-O let Black consolidate. At depth 16 e6 is the engine's first choice by a large margin.

feedback_by_move.e1g1: Castling lets Black play ...dxe5 or ...Be7 and consolidate; the engine rates it far behind e6.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a move within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16).

claims.statement: ...Bd5 is within 40 cp of the engine's top move (depth 16).

hints: Count the attackers of the pawn on e4 and of the bishop's best diagonal.
A bishop move can offer a trade and defend at the same time.
The bishop goes to the centre.
items.explain: The bishop moves to d5, where it offers a trade of the bishop on c4 and covers the e4 pawn. It is the engine's first choice at depth 16 by a wide margin.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a move within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16).

claims.statement: Nc4 is within 40 cp of the engine's top move (depth 16).

hints: Which of Black's pieces is the most active, and which white piece could challenge it?
Look at the squares c4 and e3 for the knight.
The knight goes to c4.
items.explain: The knight steps to c4 and heads for e3 or b6, away from the pawn that attacks it. It is the engine's first choice at depth 16.
